U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio decided to cancel the photo after determining that the controversy would be a distraction, according to two U.S. officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter. The meeting in Atlanta, which will otherwise go ahead as planned, is meant to set the stage for a G20 leaders’ summit hosted by President Donald Trump at his Miami golf club in December. headline: QC cops on full alert for Undas crowds
snippet: The Quezon City Police District (QCPD) will deploy personnel to cemeteries, transport terminals, churches, and other major public areas as it intensifies security measures for the observance of All Saints’ Day and All Souls’ Day. Police Brig. Gen. Christopher Olazo, QCPD acting district director, said the deployment will be supported by force multipliers as the district prepares for the expected influx of people during Undas 2026. Aside from cemeteries, columbaria, and memorial parks, police personnel will also be stationed at LRT and MRT stations, shopping malls, markets, and other major convergence areas. Police Assistance Desks (PADs) will be established in cemeteries and columbaria to assist visitors, while regular patrols will be conducted in residential communities to deter criminal activities and safeguard properties while residents are away. As part of its preparations, the QCPD has conducted coordination meetings with concerned government agencies and stakeholders, inspected transport hubs, and held a simulation exercise involving unattended baggage suspected of containing an explosive device at a bus terminal. The exercise aimed to assess emergency response capabilities and strengthen coordination among concerned agencies in handling potential security threats. The QCPD reminded the public to observe security regulations and local government guidelines, particularly the prohibition on bringing weapons and sharp objects, alcoholic beverages, cigarettes, vape products, gambling paraphernalia, flammable materials, and loud sound systems into designated areas. Residents were also advised to remain vigilant, secure their personal belongings, exercise caution in crowded places, and plan their cemetery visits accordingly. Olazo urged the public to cooperate with security personnel and immediately report emergencies or suspicious activities to the nearest police station, E911, or the Quezon City Helpline 122.

headline: Arini losses deepen to 26% as European junk bond selloff accelerates
snippet: Arini Capital Management's flagship hedge fund has lost approximately 26% this year as a selloff in Europe's riskiest corporate debt forces the $21.7bn credit manager to adopt a more defensive investment approach, according to a report by Bloomberg. The fund, which managed $7.5bn at the end of July, is on course for its first annual loss since founder Hamza Lemssouguer launched the strategy in 2022. Lemssouguer, a former Credit Suisse credit trader, has reportedly reduced new purchases to focus on managing existing positions, withdrawing a significant source of liquidity from Europe's distressed debt market. The retreat comes as European triple-C rated corporate bonds face their longest losing streak since 2018, with October potentially marking their worst monthly performance in four years. Rising interest rates, higher energy prices and concerns over corporate creditworthiness have intensified pressure on heavily indebted borrowers, while other credit hedge funds have also suffered losses. Sona Asset Management's flagship fund declined 3.1% in the first half of October, putting it on course for its worst month since launching in 2016. Arini's concentrated exposure to distressed borrowers has contributed to the drawdown, including positions in Aston Martin and Altice International. Aston Martin's bonds fell from approximately 55 cents on the dollar at the beginning of October to 47 cents by Wednesday, while debt issued by Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection has dropped below 75 cents from more than 92 cents at the end of September. Some investors have reportedly become reluctant to purchase securities in which Arini holds sizeable positions. Despite the losses, Arini continues to attract capital, having raised $1.5bn for its credit strategy and reopened the fund to existing investors. More than $400m of the new commitments was allocated at the beginning of October, with the remainder scheduled for deployment through February. The downturn marks a sharp reversal for a manager whose flagship fund returned 25.8% in 2023, 20.8% in 2024 and 8.6% in 2025. However, some credit investors believe the market dislocation could create opportunities to acquire distressed securities at attractive valuations, even as concerns grow over further losses across Europe's lowest-rated debt markets.
